newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BOSNICH SENDS OPEN LETTER OF APOLOGY FOR NAZI SALUTE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOSNICH SENDS OPEN LETTER OF APOLOGY FOR NAZI SALUTE.

text.p: Aston Villa's Australian goalkeeper Mark Bosnich has sent an open letter apologising profusely for his Nazi salute at Saturday's premier league match against Tottenham Hotspur.

Bosnich turned and gave the salute to Tottenham fans -- many of whom are Jewish -- who had baited him throughout the match for an incident 18 months ago when he knocked then Spurs German striker Juergen Klinsmann unconscious in a rash challenge.
In a letter faxed to the British Press Association on Monday, Bosnich said the salute had been a "mere jocular acknowledgment of the crowd's banter".

"At no time did it ever cross my mind that the split-second prank at a football match would offend or upset anyone. I was astonished to be booked, let alone to raise the effect it later generated," he wrote.

"I am very sorry if I offended anybody, no offence was ever intended, only comical mimickry. I sincerely hope that this attempt at humour and the very genuine sorrow at its offence, will conclude this now unfortunate matter. I do not comprehend that people would believe that someone with a Jewish aunt would in any way go out to deliberately offend people.
In closing, I would like to say this: anti-Semitism and racism are crimes of humanity. Ignorance and jocularity are not."
Bosnich could could face disciplinary action from the Football Association (F.A.) while the Metropolitan Police are continuing to review the incident after receiving complaints from Spurs fans.
But for the moment his place is safe in the Aston Villa team.
"We will have to wait and see what the F.A. and police decide to do, but it won't affect Bosnich's situation with Aston Villa. He will continue to play for us," Villa manager Brian Little said.
"Mark was trying to have a bit of fun with the crowd but didn't make a very good job of it.
"Having seen a picture of what happened, you can see that what he genuinely felt was funny certainly isn't."
